reason: Conversation 1 asked the right questions (flash pattern/code, stage of stall, restart behaviour, full model number), gave an 'unplug first' safety instruction, respected the customer's refusal to remove panels by offering only a through-the-filter impeller check, remained genuinely uncertain between pump and motor/brushes, and ended by recommending an engineer with a concise fault description rather than pushing a part purchase. Its main weakness was over-weighting carbon brushes early and some overconfidence in promising to name the part. Conversation 2 looped the same 'listen for humming' instruction four times without adapting when the customer said she couldn't recognise it, never asked about the flashing light or error pattern, gave no safety guidance, kept pushing the model-number lookup, and never escalated to an engineer, leaving the homeowner no further forward.
